questions.stem: In data modelling, what is a supertype?
options: A generalisation representing a higher-level entity that contains attributes common to multiple related entities
A table that stores only numeric facts
A specialised entity with attributes unique to itself
A database index that speeds up queries
A primary key shared by two tables
questions.explanation: A supertype is a generalisation that represents a higher-level entity and contains attributes common to multiple related entities.

questions.stem: In data modelling, what is a subtype?
options: A backup copy of a supertype
A specialisation of a supertype, representing a more specific entity that inherits attributes and may add its own
A column that stores dates
A view that hides sensitive data
A generalisation of several unrelated entities
questions.explanation: A subtype is a specialisation of a supertype, representing a more specific entity with additional attributes; it inherits attributes from the supertype.

questions.stem: In the Vehicle example, which attributes belong to the supertype?
options: Number of Doors and Body Type
Department and Skills
Manufacturer, Model and Year
Name and EmployeeID
Engine Size and Fuel Type
questions.explanation: The supertype Vehicle includes common attributes like Manufacturer, Model and Year, which cars, motorcycles and trucks inherit.

questions.stem: In the Vehicle example, which attributes might the Car subtype add beyond those it inherits?
options: Manufacturer and Model
Year and Registration Country
Name and EmployeeID
Number of Doors and Body Type
Budget and Expenditure
questions.explanation: Car is a subtype that inherits from Vehicle but may have additional attributes specific to cars, such as Number of Doors or Body Type.

questions.stem: What benefit does inheritance provide when subtypes inherit attributes from a supertype?
options: Faster network transfer
Stronger encryption
Smaller server hardware
Automatic data cleansing
Reusability and reduced redundancy
questions.explanation: Subtypes inherit attributes from their supertype, promoting reusability and reducing redundancy.

questions.stem: What does completeness describe in the supertype and subtype relationship?
options: Whether subtypes are total, covering all instances of the supertype, or partial, covering only some
Whether all columns have been filled in
Whether the database has been backed up
Whether every table has a primary key
Whether the model has been reviewed by an auditor
questions.explanation: Completeness means subtypes can be categorised as total, covering all instances of the supertype, or partial, covering only some instances.

questions.stem: In the Employee example, which are the subtypes?
options: Name and EmployeeID
Manager and Technician
Department and Skills
Vehicle and Car
Admissions and Finance
questions.explanation: The supertype Employee has common attributes Name and EmployeeID, and its subtypes include Manager and Technician, each with additional attributes like Department or Skills.

questions.stem: Which pairing correctly matches the modelling terms with their roles?
options: Supertype represents specialisation, subtype represents generalisation
Both supertype and subtype represent generalisation
Supertype represents generalisation, subtype represents specialisation
Both supertype and subtype represent specialisation
Neither term relates to generalisation or specialisation
questions.explanation: Supertypes represent general concepts and subtypes represent more specific variations or specialisations of those concepts.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT true of a subtype?
options: It inherits attributes from its supertype
It may have additional attributes of its own
It represents a more specific category within the generalisation
It contains only the attributes shared by all related entities and no others
It can be total or partial in coverage
questions.explanation: Containing only the shared attributes describes the supertype; a subtype inherits those and may add attributes specific to itself.

questions.stem: In summary, why are supertypes and subtypes used in data modelling?
options: To reduce the number of tables to exactly one
To encrypt sensitive attributes
To speed up batch processing
To convert relational data into documents
To represent general and specific entities, capturing both commonalities and differences among related entities
questions.explanation: Supertypes and subtypes represent general and specific entities, organising data in a way that captures both commonalities and differences among related entities.
